newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows Swiss Telecom funds through Mauritius.
newsitem.headline: India allows Swiss Telecom funds through Mauritius.

text.p: India has allowed Swiss Telecom PTT to route its investment into an Indian joint venture, Sterling Cellular Ltd, through Mobilwest, its Mauritian subsidiary, a government statement said on Monday.
The government has also allowed Motorola and Hongkong's Distacom to channel their investments in cellular telephone firm Modicom Network Pvt Ltd through fully-owned subsidiaries in Mauritius.
India allows foreign companies to route their investments into ventures in India through subsidiaries in Mauritius on a case-by-case basis.
India and Mauritius have signed a taxation treaty which exempts companies based in Mauritius from paying corporate tax in India.
Incorporated in Mauritius, Mobilwest is a fully-owned subsidiary of Swiss Telecom PTT.

Sterling Cellular Ltd has been granted licences to provide cellular telephone services in Delhi and three other zones under an economic liberalisation programme launched in 1991, which aims to privatise India's state-run telecommunications sector.
The government has also allowed Swiss Telecom PTT to raise its investment in Sterling Cellular Ltd to 849.3 million rupees ($23.7 million) from 735 million rupees, the statement said.
The approval will increase Swiss Telecom PTT's stake in Sterling Cellular from the present 30 percent to 32.65 percent. India's Essar group holds the majority stake in the venture.

Modicom holds the cellular licences for two Indian zones. It has an equity capital of 3.4 billion rupees. India's Modicorp holds 51 percent in Modicom, while Distacom holds 39 percent and Motorola 10 percent. ($1 = 35.77 rupees)
